the Act) challenging the judgment and order passed by the learned 3 rd Additional District Judge,
Mehsana in L.A.R. No.95 of 2002 dated 9.6.2009.

Brief facts of the case are as under:-
3.1. The land situated in village Jaidevpura, Taluka Krdi, District: Mehsana was acquired by ONGC for the purpose of project of well No.VJEC.
Notification under Section 4 of the Act was published on 18.3.2000 and the declaration under Section 6 was published on 16.5.2000.
The Land Acquisition Officer awarded award in Land Acquisition Case No.854 of 1996 - M on 23.5.2002, awarding compensation at the rate of Rs.25.50 paisa per square meter.

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The said award was challenged by the claimants by preferring Land Reference Case under Section 18 of the Act before the Reference Court.
The original claimant claimed compensation at the rate of Rs.150 per square meter.
The learned reference Court awarded compensation by determining the market value of land in question at the rate of Rs.38.25 paisa per square meter as additional compensation on 9.6.2009.

4. Learned advocate for the appellant has submitted that the learned reference Court has awarded very meagre amount of additional compensation over and above, compensation which was awarded by the Special Land Acquisition Officer.

sentences.text: It is submitted that Railway Station of Kadi village is only 3 km away from the acquired land.
It is further submitted that the claimants are residing in area known as Jaidevpura, which is a part of village Nani Kadi.
The boundaries of village Kadi and Nani Kadi is touching each other and looking to the development in the said village, the market value has been determined at a very low rate.

4.2. 
It is further submitted that for the same purpose, same land of the appellant was acquired by the present respondent in the year 1999.
Notification was published on 26.4.1999 under Section 4 of the Act.
The Section 6 notification was published on 17.10.1999.
The appellant received Rs.124 per square meter as compensation in those reference cases.
In the case where Notification under Section 4 was published on 26.4.1999, Land Acquisition Officer awarded compensation at Rs.24/- per square meter.
On challenge, learned Reference Court granted Rs.124/- per square meter as compensation.
The said award was challenged before this Court being FA No.5241 of 2008 and this Court awarded total compensation at Rs.75/- per square meter.

The claimant assailed the decision before the Hon'ble Apex Court [being Civil Appeal No.5541 of 2017 [arising out of Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.23413/2016] wherein vide order NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/18/2010 ORDER DATED: 12/08/2024 undefined dated 24.4.2017, the Hon'ble Apex Court upheld the decision of the learned reference Court.
It is thus submitted that the order of compensation was confirmed at Rs.124 per square metre in the land reference case of the same village.
It is therefore submitted that the total compensation may be awarded at the rate of Rs.124 per square meter.
4.3. It is submitted that learned reference Court has taken into consideration decision of LRC No.1206 of 2008, under which Section 4 Notification was published on 23.9.1984.
The said decision was neither produced by claimant nor by original opponents.

5. Per contra, learned advocate, Mr. Ajay R. Mehta submitted that the learned reference Court has considered the evidence on record and no interference is required in the finding of the learned reference Court.

5.1. It is further submitted that the decision which has been relied upon by the appellant is of the village Nani Kadi, whereas in the present case, the land under acquisition is of village Jaidevpura.
Learned advocate for the respondent has placed on record a copy of map which has been taken out from the Google map which is taken on record.

5.2. It is submitted that on perusal of the said map, the boundary of village Jaidevpura and boundary of village Nani Kadi are far away from each other, and even from the map, there is no mention about the village Jaidevpura .
5.3.
It is further submitted that in the land acquisition proceedings of village Merda, this Court has granted total compensation at Rs.44 per square meter.
The decision dated 6.8.2015 of the Division Bench of this Court in First Appeal No.3531 of 2011 is placed on record.

5.4. It is further submitted that In the decision of First Appeal No.3531 of 2011, the land was acquired pursuant to a notification under Section 4 dated 31.12.1998, wherein, the Land Acquisition Officer awarded compensation of the acquired land at the rate of Rs.4 per square meter.
Learned reference Court after considering the evidence, awarded additional compensation at the rate of Rs.65 per square meter.

This court vide order dated 6.8.2015 in First Appeal No.3531 of 2011,
awarded total compensation at Rs.44/- per square meter.
It is submitted that the said decision is squarely applicable to the facts of the present case.

C/FA/18/2010 ORDER DATED:
 
5.5.
In rejoinder, learned advocate, Mr. K.M. Sheth for the appellant has drawn the attention of this court of oral deposition of the original claimant which is recorded at Exh.15.
It is pointed out from the cross-examination that the claimant has deposed that the acquired land is within the village of Nani Kadi and Jaidevpura is a suburb of Nani Kadi.
It is also pointed out from the award under Section 11 of the Land Acquisition Officer that the land situated in village Nani Kadi was acquired for the purpose of project of well.

5.6 It is further pointed out that there is nothing on record to point out that the village Nani Kadi and village Jaidevpura are different villages as alleged by the learned Patel Narsinhbhai Hansrajbhai vs Special Land Acquisition Officer on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64265793/

sentences.text: From the Google Map, there is no mention of village Jaidevpura.
Hence, it can be presumed that there is no named village Jaidevpura near the vicinity of village Nani Kadi.
6. I have considered the submissions canvassed by the learned advocates for the parties and also perused the records and proceedings.
The part of being Survey No.187/5 of village Nani Kadi was acquired by ONGC for the purpose of project of well No.V.J.E.C for which Section 4 notification under the Act was published on 26.4.1999.
Declaration under Section 6 of the Act was published on NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/18/2010 ORDER DATED: 12/08/2024 undefined 17.10.1999.
The Land Acquisition Officer awarded compensation at the rate of 24/- paisa per square meter.

The said award was assailed by the original claimants by preferring land reference case under Section 18 of the Act wherein the learned Reference Court after considering the evidence, determined compensation at Rs.124 per square meter.
The said decision was assailed before this Court by First Appeal No.5241 of 2008, wherein total compensation was fixed at Rs.75/- per square meter.

6.1. The said decision was assailed before the Hon'ble Apex Court being Civil Appeal No(s) 5541 of 2017 [arising out of Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.23413 /2016)], wherein Apex Court vide order dated 24.4.2017 upheld the order of learned reference Court, who had assessed the market value of the land at the rate of Rs.124 per square meter after considering the increase of price rise at the rate of Rs.10% per year on cumulative basis.

Paras 3, 4 and 5 are as under:-
"3.Having considered the matter we are of the view that in the facts of the present case the High Court was not justified in refusing the benefit of cumulative increase to the appellant landowners.
4. The learned Reference Court while awarding compensation to the appellants relied on the notification of 1984 (i.e. dated 23 rd September, 1984) in respect of the same village wherein the landowners were granted compensation at the rate of Rs. 30/- per NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/18/2010 ORDER DATED: 12/08/2024 undefined square meter

and the same rate (i.e. Rs.30/- per square meter) has been taken as the base for awarding compensation to the appellants by granting the benefit of increase of price rise at the rate of 10% per year on cumulative basis.
The compensation awarded by the learned Reference Court i.e. Rs.124/- per square meter has been worked out on the aforesaid.
5. We do not find any error in the exercise by the learned Reference Court Interference of the High Court therefore, was not justified.

We, accordingly, interfere with the order of the High Court and set aside the same including the directions for refund of the alleged excess amount by the appellants - landowners and restore the compensation awarded by the learned Reference Court."
In the present case remaining part of claimant's land bearing Survey No.187/5 of same village has been acquired for same purpose of project of well No.VJEC.

When the remaining land of same claimant is acquired for the same purpose, there can not be seperate criteria for awarding Patel Narsinhbhai Hansrajbhai vs Special Land Acquisition Officer on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64265793/

sentences.text: In the present case, Section 4 notification is dated 18.3.2000.
The decision of First Appeal No.3531 of 2000 is pertaining to village Merda which is far away from the village Nani Kadi.

The decision in the First Appeal No.5241 of 2008 pertains to village Nani Kadi, the evidence which has been considered in the aforesaid decision and the market value which has been determined by the reference Court can be applied in the present case for the reason that the date of notification under Section 4 in both the cases is only 26.4.1999 and 18.3.2000 respectively and the difference is only 10 months and 21 days.

In my view, the parameters which have been relied upon by the learned reference Court in determining the market value at Rs.124 per square meter in the Land Acquisition Reference Case No.5360 of 2003, can be considered in determining the market value of the land in the present proceedings.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Reference Case No.5360 of 2003
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 6.3. The learned Reference Court has not properly appreciated the parameters which are required to be considered for determining the market value of the land in question.

In my view, the total compensation should be determined at the rate of Rs.124/- per square meter and the claimants are entitled to Rs.124 per square meter as total amount of compensation for the acquisition of their NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/18/2010 ORDER DATED: 12/08/2024 undefined land.
6.4. The next question which requires consideration as to from which date interest can be calculated.
The award under Section 11 is passed on 23.5.2002 by the special Land Acquisition Officer.
Relying upon the provisions contained under Section 16 of the Act which contemplates taking possession of the land by the Collector upon making an award under Section 11 of the land in question.
Section 28 of the Act also contemplates interest on excess compensation.
Section 28 of the Act provides that interest shall be paid on excess amount of compensation from the date on which the Collector took possession of the land.
Both the provisions are clear and needs no interpretation.

When the law contemplates interest to be calculated from the date of taking possession and the Collector can take possession upon passing of award under Section 11, In my view, the date of possession can be construed as 23.5.2002 which is the date of award passed under Section 11 of the Act.
Thus, claimants are entitled to interest on additional compensation from 23.5.2002.
7. Resultantly, this First Appeal is party allowed.

The judgment and order passed by 3 rd Additional District Judge, Mehsana NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/18/2010 ORDER DATED: 12/08/2024 undefined in Land Acquisition Reference Case No.95 of 2002 is hereby modified and the original claimants are entitled to Rs.124 per square meter as total compensation.
